- No documented police profiling of trans people currently.
- Some societal hostility, dated 2011 violence; 2024 says social unacceptability broadly.

No documented visitor-facing refusal or service discrimination record. No documented border friction. No demonstrated remedy/recourse (rejected recommendations; no hate-crime law).

This is a "thin data" jurisdiction with negative structural signals: socially conservative, state indifferent to anti-LGBT violence, unequal age of consent enforced. But no trans-specific visitor exposure documented. Per rule 13/thin-data extrapolation: extrapolate from structural facts.

I would place it below 0.65 (which requires documented acceptance plus remedies) and around 0.45-0.55. Our dossier lacks documented acceptance in modern terms (2024 says unacceptability), but has an old tolerance tradition? Unequal age of consent: enforced against a woman (2020 arrest) — same-sex conduct with a under-21 partner is a real criminal exposure. For a trans visitor, less direct but a trans woman with a male partner... In this legal framing, if a trans woman's documents say female, a relationship with a man is opposite-sex — but officials may not treat it that way, potentially exposing both to the same-sex age-of-consent statute. That's a real but edge-case exposure.

In a well-documented state, silence is moderately positive; here, given the government's rejection of anti-violence measures and the concealment account, silence is not positive.
